title: Anticipatory GPU reserve: sliding-window KV-pressure forecasts and soft-commit ledger
creator: Lena Park
description: Problem: sudden tenant bursts and skewed request-size distributions cause reactive KV eviction and weight offloads that spike tail latency. Current memory budgeting is reactive (evict-when-full) and does not reserve predictive headroom for KV growth during continuous batching. Goal: design and implement an anticipatory GPU reserve policy that uses a short-term sliding-window forecast of KV pressure and batch composition to create 'elastic headroom pockets' via a soft-commit ledger. The policy should reduce incremental evictions during transient bursts, preserve SLO for 99th percentile latency, and minimize additional reserved memory overhead across fleet.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Forecast agent runs in production agents with <5ms median CPU overhead per allocation decision.
2) Observed decrease in KV-triggered evictions by >=35% on measured tenant burst simulations.
3) 99th percentile latency for latency-sensitive routes improves or remains within SLO (no regressions) after rollout.
4) New soft-commit ledger can be toggled per-pool and per-tenant with metric visibility in the Console.
5) Automated canary shows no increase in OOMs or failed allocations over 7-day window.
technical_notes:
Core idea: combine two signals — short-term KV-growth-rate (dKV/dt) sampled from the last N requests per GPU and batch-size composition histogram — into a probabilistic headroom forecast. Use an exponentially-weighted moving quantile (EWQ) to estimate a 95th percentile KV delta over a 30s horizon. Compute a recommended reserve R = base_model_weights + EWQ_KV + safety_margin( alpha, load_variance ). Implement soft-commit ledger: instead of hard-reserving physical memory, record logical reservations with aging and preemption priority. When workloads approach physical constraints, soft reservations can be evicted following priority and age. Key knobs: EWQ window length, quantile target, safety_margin function, soft-commit aging policy, preemption classes (system, tenant-critical, opportunistic). Forecast jitter reduction: apply hysteresis and minimum hold time to avoid flip-flopping during noisy signals. Coordinate with batcher: expose reservation hints so batcher avoids creating super-sized batches that would blow predicted headroom.
Implementation considerations: we will build components in the allocation agent (C++) and a lightweight forecasting microservice (Go) that can run co-located with allocation agent or as a sidecar. Telemetry surfaces: per-GPU forecast, reservation ledger state, soft-commit evictions, predicted vs actual KV growth.
Memory accounting model: ledger entries map to reservation tags (weights, kv, activations) with string identifiers. Eviction ordering uses (reservation_priority, age, reservation_size) comparator.
Safety: fall back to current allocator when forecasting service becomes unavailable.
implementation_plan:
1) Prototype forecast algorithm in Python using production trace samples (by 2026-03-18).
2) Implement EWQ estimator and simulate on historical traces to choose hyperparams (by 2026-03-24).
3) Implement soft-commit ledger in allocator runtime (C++) with feature flag gating (by 2026-04-01).
4) Add telemetry and Console dashboard tiles: forecast vs actual, ledger health, soft-commit evictions (by 2026-04-03).
5) Canary: enable on a small cohort of low-risk tenants and a single region for 7 days (by 2026-04-05).
6) Gradual rollout with metric guardrails and automatic rollback on regression (post-canary).
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): 5% of production pools, tenant opt-in, monitor for 7 days. Phase B (regional expansion): enable for one additional region at 25% pool coverage. Phase C (global): ramp with automated detection and rollback. Toggle points: forecast TTL, safety_margin multiplier. Rollout gates: soft-commit eviction rate, 99th latency, OOM counts. Provide per-tenant opt-out for critical customers via Console flag.
testing_plan: Unit tests for EWQ estimator, ledger bookkeeping, and comparator logic. Integration tests: allocation agent with simulated forecast sidecar. Load tests: replay spike traces (up to 5x baseline burst) in staging and measure eviction counts. Long-run soak test: 72-hour run with synthetic diurnal patterns to detect drift. Chaos test: kill forecast service and verify fallback allocator behavior.
metrics: Primary: KV-eviction-rate (evictions/min), 99th-latency-ms for latency-sensitive routes, OOM count per-pool. Secondary: forecast-error (|predicted_kv_delta - observed|), soft-commit-reserved-memory, soft-commit-eviction-rate, CPU overhead per-allocation-decision. Dashboards: per-pool and fleet-level heatmaps and time series.
risks:
1) Over-reserving memory increases idle capacity and unit cost. Mitigation: tune safety_margin and decay reservations automatically.
2) Forecast instability causes oscillation in reservations. Mitigation: hysteresis, minimum hold time, and prioritization of admission control.
3) Ledger complexity introduces new failure modes. Mitigation: feature-flagged rollout, exhaustive unit tests, and automatic fallback.
4) Telemetry volume growth. Mitigation: sample telemetry and roll-up counters.
